name: DC veterans: Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs for claims help
organization: District of Columbia, Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs (MOVA)
description: Free help with federal VA claims and benefits from MOVA’s District Veteran Service Officers, plus outreach, community resources and District veteran programs for veterans and their families.
next_step: Call MOVA at 202-724-5454 (weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) or use its online intake form.
constraints: Call ahead; the office is in One Judiciary Square.

name: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (Aging and Disability Resource Center)
organization: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
description: The District’s aging agency and Aging and Disability Resource Center: senior centers, meals, transportation, in-home support, caregiver help and legal services for residents 60 and older and adults with disabilities. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call DACL at 202-724-5626 (TTY 711), weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (DC SHIP)
organization: DC Department of Aging and Community Living, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
description: Free, unbiased health insurance counseling for Medicare beneficiaries, families and caregivers in the District from DACL’s SHIP counselors.
next_step: Call the SHIP Helpline at 202-727-8370 or email ship.dacl@dc.gov. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: The helpline keeps limited weekday hours; leave a message if no one answers.

name: DC Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Legal Counsel for the Elderly, Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman; DACL Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and community residence facilities, and for people receiving EPD waiver services at home. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults, 24 hours a day.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 202-434-2190 or email DCOmbuds@aarp.org. To report abuse, call Adult Protective Services at 202-541-3950, 24 hours a day. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: VA health care in the District
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Washington DC Healthcare System
description: District veterans are served by the Washington DC VA Medical Center, 50 Irving Street NW (202-745-8000), and its community clinics.
next_step: Call 202-745-8000 for appointments; after hours, ask the operator for the administrator on duty. Not enrolled yet? Ask MOVA for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

source_evidence.title: VA Washington DC health care: Contact us
source_evidence.scope: Washington DC VA Medical Center, 50 Irving Street NW; local 202-745-8000; search excerpt.

name: DC Center for Independent Living
organization: The DC Center for Independent Living (DCCIL)
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 2600 12th Street NE, Washington, DC 20018; TTY 202-388-0277.
Other offices: 2901 14th St NW, 202-280-6899; Anacostia, 2443 Good Hope Road SE, 202-889-5802.

name: Housing Counseling Services, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 14-ZZ-313): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
